prompt:
사용자 요청 원문:
좋아. 이제 인스턴스를 다시 켜고 첫 태스크를 만들어보자.
필요한 CLI 인증부터 확인하고, 로봇 조립·데이터센터 정비 분야에서 산업 근거가 있고 기존 제출과 겹치지 않는 후보를 골라 제출 전 검토 단계까지 진행해줘.

확정된 제작 조건:
- Category: Impact on AI timelines. 로봇 조립 또는 데이터센터 정비 중 실제 산업에서 자동화할 의미가 있는 물리 조작 하나를 선택한다.
- 제조사 설치·정비 매뉴얼, 공식 조립 절차, 공개 설계, 실제 작업 영상·보고서의 원문으로 작업과 장비 형상·치수·절차를 입증한다. 추측이나 가상 산업 용도를 만들어내지 않는다.
- 여러 후보를 비교하고 목적·물리 기술·성공 조건의 신규성과 로봇의 어려운 조작 능력을 함께 검토하여 하나만 제작한다. 조작의 어려움은 극단적일 필요는 없지만 단순 물체 옮기기를 산업 이름만 바꾼 작업은 피한다.
- 모든 분야의 기존 accepted/pending/open 제출 및 우리 팀 기존 제출, 지정된 기존 벤치마크와 비교한다. 기하·색상·배치·시작 자세·난도만 다른 것은 새 태스크가 아니다. 선정 시점 및 완성 후 다시 전수 비교한다. 불확실한 중복을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 가능한 강체 PhysX 작업을 선택한다. 기존의 검증된 연성 에셋이 없다면 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 실제 산업 장비의 형태와 중요한 물리 제약을 재현한다. 공개 에셋은 라이선스·출처·치수를 기록하고 적합하지 않으면 직접 제작한다.
- objective와 환경·부품 물리를 먼저 완성·진단한 뒤 YAM 전체 데모·채점기를 연결한다. 물체 순간이동/상태 덮어쓰기로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 관련 부품 파손·금지 동작·실패·부분 점수와 성공 유지 시간을 수치로 평가한다.
- 실제 simulator 측정·두 번의 full-score YAM 데모·실패/부분 점수 대조군·영상/원시 trace 및 깨끗한 경로 재현 검사를 수행한다. 미검증 수치와 성공을 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
- 모든 제작·검증을 마친 후에만 Dream 최종 평가 episode 1회. 실패나 불명 결과도 자동 재평가하지 않는다. 누적 $20 ledger를 준수하고 인증이 없으면 제작을 보존한 뒤 평가 대기한다.
- 결과는 이 run의 새로운 origin 브랜치에 보존한다. 원본 매뉴얼 전체/인증 정보는 공개하지 않는다. 50MB/file 또는 100MB checkpoint 초과는 먼저 보고한다.
- 완료 후 GPU를 stop하고 제출 전 검토 보고서·영상·채점 결과를 제공한다. 실제 미디어 업로드·대회 PR·승인은 하지 않는다.
- 기존 feature/close-snack-bag checkout 및 robocurve-snack-film 인스턴스는 별개 작업이므로 건드리지 않는다.

selected.title: Depin a Mini-Fit Jr. 5556 terminal from a 5557 housing
selected.objective: With a de-energized four-circuit Mini-Fit Jr. 39012040/5557 receptacle fixed in a service fixture, guide the HT60630B extraction tool around the selected 5556 terminal, depress both locking tangs, maintain tool engagement, push the wire toward the tool if needed, and then pull the wire and terminal from the rear without releasing neighboring terminals or damaging the reusable housing.
skills: precision tool-tip alignment with housing guide slots
constrained dual-blade insertion around a recessed contact
contact and force control while depressing two locking tangs
bimanual coordination between sustained tool engagement and opposite-side wire pull
regrasping a slender tool and wire
avoidance of neighboring terminals and housing walls
selected.success_conditions: Research-stage rubric: the designated terminal and its wire must exit through the rear of its original cavity through robot-applied contact forces; the housing stays fixed and reusable; all other terminals remain fully retained; the wire remains attached to the extracted terminal; and the tool, housing, insulation, contact body, and adjacent terminals show no prohibited displacement or damage. Success must persist for 3 seconds after both grippers release the extracted terminal and tool. Score zero for extracting the wrong or an additional terminal, pulling the wire out of its crimp, breaking or permanently displacing the housing, bypassing the tangs, or teleporting/welding/state-overwriting the terminal. Partial credit may distinguish correct tool entry, both tangs depressed, and partial rearward withdrawal, but no unmeasured numerical force or damage threshold is asserted. Development is blocked until the rigid tang/contact abstraction passes insertion, retention, overload, and reset tests with measured proxy hardware.
selected.industrial_value: Molex identifies HT60630B as tooling specifically designed to extract crimped Mini-Fit terminals, while TE identifies terminal extraction without housing damage as important to OEM and aftermarket rework and repair. Molex also lists Mini-Fit connectors for commercial-cleaning-robot drive and motion-control interconnects. This supports harness rework as an industrial manipulation objective, without claiming that every 39012040 housing is installed in that particular robot application.
selected.dexterity: High but feasible. The robot must enter narrow housing slots with two blades outside the contact, recognize terminal contact, maintain tang-depressing engagement, optionally unload the tangs by pushing the wire forward, and coordinate an opposing gentle pull. This is materially different from mating a completed connector or operating its external latch.

evidence.quote: This tool is designed to extract crimped Mini-Fit series terminals from their housings.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 1, FEATURES

evidence.quote: Use the slots located on the inside of the housing to guide the extraction tool blades into the housing until contact is made with terminal.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 2, OPERATION, step 2

evidence.quote: If the terminal locking tabs are still not totally depressed, hold on tight to the wire and push it toward the extraction tool.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 2, OPERATION, step 4

evidence.quote: Grasp the terminal by the wire, and gently pull it out from the housing.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 2, OPERATION, step 5

evidence.quote: Note: When a terminal is removed in this manner the locking tangs are damaged and the terminal is not reusable.
evidence.locator: Extraction Tool HT60630B for Mini-Fit Series Terminals, page 2, note below Terminal and Housing Application Chart

evidence.quote: Our insertion tools and extraction tools are designed to respectively insert and extract a terminal from the connector housing without damaging the terminal or housing—a key criteria in quality wire processing that is especially important for rework and repair at the OEM and in the after-market.
evidence.locator: TE Connectivity, Insertion and Extraction Tools for Wire Processing, High-Precision Insertion and Extraction Tools section
Molex part 39012040 product page, Physical Specifications

evidence.quote: Motors and motion systems in cleaning robots need vibration-resistant connectors to maintain reliable power and signal transmission despite exposure to moisture and cleaning chemicals.
evidence.locator: Molex, Connectors and Cable Assemblies for Commercial Cleaning Robots, Drive and Motion Control Connectors section

selected.asset_plan: Use the documented four-circuit 39012040/5557 housing and a compatible 5556 terminal only; do not mix the 5378 geometry or another extraction-tool series. Build dimensioned rigid housing, terminal, crimp barrel, wire, and HT60630B proxy meshes from the acquired Molex drawing plus measurements of reference parts. Represent each terminal tang as a constrained articulated rigid leaf with calibrated detent and irreversible damage state rather than a deformable solver. The wire may initially be a short rigid handle for component-physics tests; any later segmented cable must use an already validated YAM-compatible model. Validate blade clearance, outside-contact guidance, tang release, retained-state pull resistance, extraction after release, neighbor retention, overload damage, and reset repeatability before attempting a full robot demo in pinned Isaac Sim 6.1.0/YAM 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730. No task object may be teleported or welded to produce extraction.
selected.risk: Medium-high implementation risk. The acquired sources establish procedure, pitch, compatible families, intended tooling, and terminal non-reusability, but do not provide blade thickness, tang stiffness, release force, pull-out force, or allowable housing-load limits. Those values require measured reference hardware. The catalog text screen found no direct depin/terminal-extraction objective, but this is not conclusive semantic proof; the complete accepted, pending, open, team, and benchmark comparison must be repeated after the objective and physics are implemented.

comparisons.objective: Extract and recover a trapped spacer with a pusher versus depinning one connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-tool pushing and pick-place versus dual-blade tang depression and coordinated wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Spacer nested and pusher parked versus selected terminal removed with housing, wire crimp, and neighbors preserved.
comparisons.reason: Generic tool-assisted extraction is shared, but the contact mechanics and required end state differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Select a wrench, release a captive nut, and open an arm versus depinning a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-size selection and rotary torque versus recessed blade insertion, tang depression, and axial pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut released without rounding, arm open, tools returned, 20-second hold versus selective terminal removal and 3-second release hold.
comparisons.reason: Fastener selection and rotary release do not test connector-terminal latch disengagement.

comparisons.objective: Remove a battery service plug and busbars in a safe order versus extracting one crimp terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plug removal and collision-safe busbar handling versus fine dual-blade insertion and simultaneous tool-wire withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Service plug removed before busbars, then bars safely trayed versus one terminal out with housing and neighbors intact.
comparisons.reason: Both involve electrical-component removal, but their mechanisms, sequencing, and final states are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Release a spring clamp and recover its screwdriver versus depinning a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp actuation and tool recovery versus recessed tang depression with sustained tool engagement and wire pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Screwdriver held by the left gripper without drop or base motion versus terminal removed without wrong-terminal release or damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared release-and-pull primitives alone do not establish overlap; the tested contact strategy differs.

comparisons.objective: Route, buckle, and tighten a child-seat harness versus depinning a rigid connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable webbing routing, buckle latching, and tensioning versus rigid-tool insertion and latch release.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct untwisted routing, latched buckle and clip, fit and hold versus selective terminal extraction with neighboring contacts retained.
comparisons.reason: The material mechanics, manipulation sequence, and functional outcome are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Route a connected cable between posts and secure its final clip versus remove a terminal from a connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual slack management and clip insertion versus dual-blade tang depression and coordinated extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Preserve the existing fixing, follow the route, seat the final clip, release and hold versus remove only the designated terminal without damage.
comparisons.reason: This record tests cable routing and retention, not terminal depinning.

comparisons.objective: Sort cubes while yielding shared space to a person's hand versus depinning a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed collision avoidance and resumed pick-place versus close-tolerance blade insertion and force-controlled release.
comparisons.success_condition: No safety-envelope violation and all cubes sorted versus selective terminal removal with component integrity.

comparisons.objective: Even wire tips and twist on a splice connector versus extract a crimp terminal from a housing.

comparisons.success_condition: Tips even, splice snug, and conductors retained versus one terminal removed while its crimp and housing remain intact.

comparisons.physical_skill: Release-control hold, slot/lug alignment, quarter-turn locking, hooking, and gross pull versus dual-blade slot guidance and opposing fine wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool remains locked and cartridge reaches the tray versus contact exits its cavity without damage or neighbor release.
comparisons.reason: Both use a tool to retrieve an item, but the record primarily tests tool-head assembly and hook retrieval; it does not test terminal tang release. Rubric is detailed.

comparisons.objective: Steer a laser with two mirrors while safely blocking the beam during adjustment; candidate performs mechanical terminal extraction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mirror placement/orientation and beam-block sequencing versus contact-rich insertion, tang depression, and bimanual load control.
comparisons.success_condition: Beam reaches detector through both mirrors without unsafe exposure versus selected terminal is physically removed intact.
comparisons.reason: Optical alignment and safety sequencing are unrelated to connector depinning mechanics. No material record fields are missing.

comparisons.objective: Position and secure two snowboard bindings to a specified stance; candidate extracts a connector contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-part pose alignment and screw fastening versus narrow-slot tool insertion and internal detent release under tension.
comparisons.success_condition: Bindings have specified spacing/orientation and are secured versus one terminal exits while surrounding connector geometry is preserved.
comparisons.reason: Different assembly scale, fastening mechanism, and success state. Record setup and scoring are populated.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both sides of a knife on a whetstone; candidate depins an electrical terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain blade angle and contact during repeated strokes versus align twin extraction blades, depress tangs, and coordinate push–pull loads.
comparisons.success_condition: Required sharpening coverage with knife safely placed versus correct terminal extracted without prohibited damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared force control is generic; the contact trajectories and tested outcomes are materially different. Record rubric is present.

comparisons.objective: Spread a circlip, install it in a shaft groove, and verify seating; candidate releases and extracts a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pliers-tip engagement, controlled ring expansion, groove seating, and rotational check versus guided dual-blade insertion and sustained tang depression during pullout.
comparisons.success_condition: Circlip squarely retained without overstretch versus designated terminal removed with housing and neighbors retained.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate spring-like retention features, but one installs an exposed removable ring while the candidate releases two recessed integral tangs. These are meaningfully different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Bleed a brake caliper with correctly sequenced pedal and bleeder-valve cycles; candidate performs connector-terminal extraction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual valve/pedal timing, repeated cycling, and fluid-state control versus precision blade insertion and opposing mechanical extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Air removed while the bleeder is closed before pedal return versus correct contact removed without connector damage.
comparisons.reason: Different mechanism, temporal procedure, and physical endpoint. Record setup and scoring are present.

comparisons.objective: Press two opposite-sense drawer-slide releases while pulling the drawer free; candidate depresses two terminal tangs while pulling a wire/contact free.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual external lever actuation and large drawer pull versus a single fine tool’s dual blades inserted around a recessed contact plus opposite-side wire handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer fully removed and set down versus only the selected terminal removed with its crimp and housing intact.
comparisons.reason: The release-and-pull pattern overlaps, but the candidate tests millimetric tool insertion, bilateral tang engagement within one cavity, and wire/contact preservation—abilities absent from the drawer task.

comparisons.objective: Scribe a shelf profile against an uneven wall; candidate removes a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a shelf while tracing a compass continuously along a surface versus constrained extraction-tool insertion and detent-force control.
comparisons.success_condition: Continuous accurate scribe line with tools cleared versus designated terminal extracted without collateral displacement or damage.
comparisons.reason: Different objective and contact mechanics; bimanual stabilization alone is generic. Record rubric is populated.

comparisons.objective: Seat an add-on PCB onto two rows of header pins without bending them; candidate extracts a crimp terminal from a housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Parallel multi-pin alignment and controlled board insertion versus twin-blade guidance outside one contact, tang depression, and rearward extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully seated with all pins straight versus selected terminal removed while adjacent terminals remain seated.
comparisons.reason: Both concern electrical connectors, but one tests array insertion and pin protection while the other tests latch release and depinning. Complete record details establish the distinction.

comparisons.objective: Place three consumer devices on their respective charging positions; candidate performs connector rework.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object pose placement and charging-contact alignment versus fine extraction-tool insertion and bimanual force sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: All devices remain charging after release versus one designated terminal remains extracted after release with no damage.
comparisons.reason: Charging placement does not test latch release, insertion around a recessed contact, or extraction. Record setup and scoring are present.

comparisons.objective: Hold a graphics-card slot latch and lift the card into a tray; candidate releases a terminal’s two locking tangs and pulls the contact from its cavity.
comparisons.physical_skill: External latch hold plus large rigid-card extraction versus guided dual-blade insertion around a recessed contact, possible forward unloading, and opposite-side wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Graphics card removed and placed in tray versus only the selected terminal and attached wire removed with housing and neighboring contacts preserved.
comparisons.reason: This has the strongest semantic overlap, but it tests an accessible single slot latch and board removal; the candidate tests bilateral internal tang engagement, fine tool alignment, and crimp-preserving wire extraction. Both rubrics are sufficiently specified.

comparisons.objective: Discharge a capacitor with a two-pin tool before removing a PSU board; candidate uses a dual-blade tool to depin one connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align two pins to exposed pads, sustain electrical contact, then perform board removal versus insert blades into housing guide slots, mechanically depress tangs, and coordinate wire extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Verified discharge precedes safe board placement in a box versus correct terminal exits its cavity without damage or neighbor release.
comparisons.reason: Both use two-pronged tools in electronics service, but one tests timed pad contact and safety sequencing while the candidate tests internal mechanical latch release. Record setup/scoring are present; candidate force limits remain explicitly unmeasured.
